As Taika Waititi ‘s latest directorial effort gets its time in the sun, he has some choice words for critics attempting to rain on his parade.
On Saturday, the Oscar winner boasted about Klara and the Sun ‘s 78% Rotten Tomatoes audience score (now at 73%), while slamming the “sad lost souls” who gave the movie a negative review, contributing to its 26% critics rating.
How ‘Klara and the Sun’ Got Blotted Out at the Box Office

“I haven’t read a review of anything aimed at me or my peers in almost 15 years. But I do listen to the people,” he prefaced on Instagram .
“So this Halloween, let’s spare a thought for those sad lost souls who couldn’t achieve their dreams of becoming artists, and thus became critics. The same people who also hated Jojo Rabbit ,” added Waititi. “Irrelevant. Out of touch. Obsolete. In the bin.” Watch on Deadline
In Deadline’s review , Damon White wrote of the Sony Pictures adaptation, “Taiki Waititi should be a snug-as-a-bug fit for Kazuo Ishiguro’s dystopian — or is it? — 2021 novel, given the director’s affinity for a very particular and peculiar kind of reality-based cringe comedy. But Klara just doesn’t deliver on any of the fronts it promises.”
Meanwhile, Waititi might have flown too close to the sun with the film’s reported $20M budget, opening last weekend to $701K domestic . Following the negative reviews out of BFI this month, Sony cut the film’s wide release to 880 theaters in the US.
Based on Kazuo Ishiguro’s 2021 dystopian novel, Klara and the Sun stars Jenna Ortega as the titular android, who is purchased as an “Artificial Friend” for gravely ill teenager Josie (Mia Tharia), whose family is mourning the death of her older sister Sal.

Anonymous on November 1, 2026 2:18 pm Virtually all the Negative Reviews I read complained about the changes in tone and and a couple key elements from the book. I completely understand the impulse of loving a book so much that you can’t help but reject the adaptation. After the first critic wrote this you couldn’t post a review saying you didn’t read the book without sounding dumb or unprofessional so everybody parroted the same complaint. This snowballed and lead to that big green splattered tomato on Rotten Tomatoes and subsequently a lot of the audience saying I’ll wait til it comes out on streaming. I would be interested in knowing how many of the critics actually read the book. That said for the rest of us that didn’t read the book can’t we just enjoy the film on it’s own merits? I think that’s why you see such a difference in the Critics score versus the audience score and can understand Taika’s frustration. Also it’s not like he pulled a Stanley Kubrick’s The Shining and just wholesale discarded much of the book. Ishiguro was a producer on the film and worked with Taika throughout the process accepting some of the changes while acknowledging that the book was ‘Bleak’. Reply Reply to
